reminder: A lattice is modular if it obeys the modular law: when $a\le c$, then $a\vee(b\wedge c)=(a\vee b)\wedge c$.
definition: A [lattice](c:lattice) $L$ is modular if $a\le c$ implies $a\vee(b\wedge c)=(a\vee b)\wedge c$ for all $a,b,c\in L$. Equivalently, for each pair $x,y$ the map $z\mapsto z\vee x$ is a bijection from $[x\wedge y,y]$ to $[x,x\vee y]$.
examples: The lattice of subgroups of an abelian group is modular.
The divisor lattice of a positive integer is modular.
Non-example: the pentagon lattice $N_5$ is not modular.

reminder: The torus is the product of circles, or the quotient $\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$.
definition: The $n$-torus is the [manifold](c:manifold) $\mathbb{T}^n=\mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$, which is the product of $n$ copies of the [circle](c:circle). It is compact, and a function on it is the same as a function on $\mathbb{R}^n$ with period $1$ in each variable.
examples: The circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ is the 1-torus.
The surface of a doughnut is the 2-torus.
Non-example: the sphere $S^2$ is not a torus, because its fundamental group is trivial.

reminder: A lift of a degree-one circle map is a monotone map $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ with $F(x+1)=F(x)+1$.
definition: A monotone [function](c:monotone-function) $F:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a lift of a degree-one circle map if $F(x+1)=F(x)+1$ for all $x$. It descends to a map of the [circle](c:circle) $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ that turns once.
examples: The shift $F(x)=x+a$ is a lift.
The map $F(x)=x+a+\epsilon\sin(2\pi x)$ with small $\epsilon$ is a lift.
Non-example: $F(x)=2x$ is not a lift, because $F(x+1)=F(x)+2$.

reminder: Currying turns a function of two arguments into a function of one argument that returns a function.
definition: Currying is the bijection between functions $A\times B\to C$ and functions $A\to (B\to C)$. Each $f$ goes to $a\mapsto f(a,\cdot)$. In a [closed monoidal category](c:closed-monoidal-category) it is the adjunction behind the [exponential object](c:exponential-object).
examples: The addition map $(a,b)\mapsto a+b$ becomes $a\mapsto(b\mapsto a+b)$.
In topology, continuous maps $X\times Y\to Z$ correspond to continuous maps $X\to C(Y,Z)$ for a locally compact Hausdorff $Y$.
Non-example: a map from $A$ to $B$ with one argument has no currying, because it has no second argument.

reminder: A deterministic automaton has a finite set of states and, for each state and input letter, exactly one next state.
definition: A deterministic automaton is a tuple $(S,\Sigma,\delta,s_0,F)$ of a state set $S$, an alphabet $\Sigma$, a transition map $\delta:S\times\Sigma\to S$, a start state $s_0$ and accepting states $F\subseteq S$. It is a [finite automaton](c:finite-automaton) when $S$ is finite. It accepts a word when the run ends in $F$. Such words form a [regular language](c:regular-language).
examples: A two-state automaton that tracks the parity of the number of $1$ letters.
The automaton for words that end in $ab$.
Non-example: a machine that may have two next states for one input is non-deterministic, not deterministic.

reminder: The evaluation map sends a pair $(f,x)$ to the value $f(x)$.
definition: For sets or spaces $X$ and $Y$, the evaluation map is $\mathrm{ev}:C(X,Y)\times X\to Y$ with $\mathrm{ev}(f,x)=f(x)$. In a [closed monoidal category](c:closed-monoidal-category) it is the counit of the adjunction that defines the [exponential object](c:exponential-object).
examples: For $X=Y=\mathbb{R}$, $\mathrm{ev}(\sin,\pi/2)=1$.
In the [compact-open topology](c:compact-open-topology) the evaluation map is continuous when $X$ is locally compact Hausdorff.
Non-example: the map $f\mapsto f'$ is not an evaluation map, because it returns a function.

reminder: The heat kernel is the fundamental solution of the heat equation, a Gaussian in the space variable.
definition: On $\mathbb{R}$, the heat kernel is $p_t(x)=(4\pi t)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/(4t)}$ for $t>0$. It is the [fundamental solution](c:fundamental-solution) of the [heat equation](c:heat-equation) $u_t=u_{xx}$. The solution with initial value $f$ is the convolution $u(t,\cdot)=p_t*f$.
examples: $\int p_t(x)\,dx=1$ for every $t>0$.
The Fourier transform of $p_t$ is $e^{-t\xi^2}$.
Non-example: the function $x\mapsto e^{-x^2}$ without the factor $t$ is one time slice, not the whole kernel.

reminder: A Hölder triple is a triple of exponents $p,q,r$ with $1/p+1/q=1/r$.
definition: Three exponents $p,q,r\in[1,\infty]$ form a Hölder triple if $\frac1p+\frac1q=\frac1r$. Then $\|fg\|_r\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q$ for $f\in L^p$ and $g\in L^q$, with the [Lp space](c:lp-space).
examples: $(2,2,1)$ is a Hölder triple: Cauchy-Schwarz.
$(p,p',1)$ with $1/p+1/p'=1$ is the classical case.
Non-example: $(2,3,1)$ is not a Hölder triple, because $1/2+1/3=5/6\neq 1$.
